generic: {Word is the east highway has been quiet for weeks.|They say the road out east has been dead quiet.|Nobody's seen a single truck on the east road all month.} {A little too quiet, if you ask me.|The mile markers past the fourth one are counting backwards now.|Even the bandits packed up and left.}

{Prices went up again across the board.|Cost of living just doubled overnight.|Taxes jumped again without any warning.} {Nobody will admit who signed the order.|The new figure in the tax ledger is written as one long unpronounceable word.|Good luck paying rent this month.}

{Somebody saw weird lights flickering over the water three nights running.|The fishermen claim strange glowing shapes have been hovering over the bay.|There are lights out on the water after dark.} {Same three nights, same weird frequency.|Probably another illegal salvage barge.|Nobody wants to go check it out.}

{The town well has tasted like {iron|stale blood|crude oil|battery acid} since spring.|The water supply tastes like rust and chemicals.|Don't drink the tap water unless you boil it twice.} {Ask five locals and they'll each blame a different faction.|The council says it's within safety standards, which means it's toxic.|The water board denies everything, as usual.}

{There's hiring going on at the old shipyard again.|The abandoned rail yard is looking for workers.|Someone reopened the old warehouse down by the tracks.} {Nobody who goes in talks about what they're building.|The workers come back humming the exact same creepy tune.|High pay, but nobody lasts more than a month.}

{A drifter rolled through last week paying for drinks in counterfeit coin.|Some stranger paid the tavern tab with coins nobody recognized.|There's weird money circulating in the district.} {The faces stamped on the metal were still blinking the next morning.|The bartender took them anyway, because money is money.|Probably minted in a dimension that collapsed on Tuesday.}

{Half the town swears the church bell rang at the wrong hour.|The clock tower chimed thirteen times yesterday.|The bells rang during the middle of the night.} {The other half swears the bells haven't rung in years.|Nobody wants to climb the tower and check the mechanism.|Just another temporal glitch to ignore.}

{The town watch changed their patrol routes without notice.|The guards started walking their patrols in reverse.|The constables doubled the gate watch.} {That never happens unless someone important messed up.|They won't say what they're looking for, but they're keeping their hands on their holsters.|Standard municipal paranoia.}

{An entire trade caravan turned back before reaching the mountain pass.|The supply convoy refused to cross the valley.|The haulers dumped their cargo and bolted.} {The drivers who came back claim they met themselves on the road coming the other way.|Nobody is taking that pass until the weather clears.|Just another day on the trade route.}

{Something broke into the grain storehouse last night.|The bakery storage got ransacked again.|Someone raided the supply depot.} {The mayor is blaming stray dogs, but dogs don't pick padlocks and neatly fold the sacks.|Definitely an inside job.|Good luck getting a straight answer from the guards.}

{The Omega Tower unlocked its blast doors on its own the night the old world ended.|The Tower gates swung wide open years ago.|Nobody has managed to seal the Tower doors since the collapse.} {Thousands go in every year; only the stubborn ones come back.|It's basically a vertical death trap.|Keep your distance unless you're feeling suicidal.}

{Keep your vehicle under eighty if you value your skin.|Drive over eighty and you'll get sucked straight into a time bubble.|Speed limits around here aren't for safety; they're for keeping your timeline intact.} {Go too fast and you'll be reliving Tuesday for the rest of your life.|The road patrol won't pull you over; they'll just watch you disappear.|Slow down and live.}

{A trucker came through with a carrier pigeon in a cage and an encrypted flash drive on its leg.|There's a courier running birds between the dimensional bubbles.|Old-school pigeon post is the only thing that crosses the anomaly zones.} {The postal service collapsed, but the birds still fly.|Ten credits a message, no receipts.|Smartest courier in the province.}

{The old prospector swears magic is seeping out of the oil reserves.|They say refined petro-fuel has leylines running right through it.|That's why they keep drilling deeper into the bedrock.} {The drillers are careful not to swear near the borehole.|Touch the crude oil and your fingertips tingle for a week.|High profit, high hazard.}

{Someone dug up a piece of the dead Father's statue in a field two counties over.|A farmer unearthed a relic from the old regime while plowing.|There's a piece of holy wreckage sitting in a barn nearby.} {Whoever touches the stone starts displaying weird powers overnight.|The Vatican dispatched an audit team to confiscate it.|Grab it before the inquisitors show up.}

{Cast a spell with an unclosed syntax tag and the universe bills you double.|Mages are getting fined by the laws of thermodynamics for sloppy chanting.|Speak a ward out of turn and you'll cough up sparks for a week.} {It starts in your vocal cords and burns its way down.|Guild bureaucracy at its finest.|Stick to mechanical tools.}

{Rome is suspended eight hundred meters off the ground these days.|The Citadel floats high above the ruins, completely cut off from the peasants.|The Vatican fortress hovers in the clouds, armed to the teeth.} {Their railguns shoot at anything flying higher than a kite.|Don't look up with binoculars unless you want a laser pointer on your forehead.|Aristocrats love their altitude.}

{There hasn't been a clean rocket launch out of Taranto in months.|Orbital debris is grinding the launch vehicles to pieces.|The spaceport is taking volunteer pilots for zero pay.} {Half the rockets detonate before reaching low orbit.|The scrap falling back to earth is ruining the olive groves.|Space travel is officially for suckers.}

{Satellite imagery shows the western continents are warping out of shape.|The coastlines look like they were drawn by an amateur with a dull crayon.|The maps don't match the terrain anymore.} {Same cities, same miserable traffic, completely wrong geography.|Cartographers gave up and started drinking.|Just follow the painted road signs.}

{The goblins crawled out of a deep borehole back in the seventies and set up shop.|There's a clan of subterranean miners living in the old shafts.|They paint their faces before every brawl and sing loud tavern songs.} {Good luck evicting them; they own the local union.|They sell cheap scrap metal if you bring good booze.|Tough crowd, but honest traders.}

{Don't pull any shady stunts in front of a witness.|She sees every infraction, calculates the fine, and sends a bounty hunter.|Commit a crime in public and you're booked before you hit the corner.} {The court is automated and has zero mercy.|Keep your head down or get your alibi notarized.|Eris is always watching the ledger.}

{Every banknote in your pocket carries the Director's name more times than a holy scripture.|The paper currency is basically an autographed corporate receipt.|Think about who's getting rich off every transaction.} {Inflation is a joke, but the interest rates are very real.|Spend it before the ink fades.|The banks always win.}

{The Tower has stood since ninety-two.|They say the Tower went up in ninety-two and never came down.|Nobody alive remembers the sky here without the Tower in it.} {It holds the ninety-two dimensions together the way a flag holds a sandwich.|Something has to keep the ninety-two dimensions stacked, and that is it.|Nobody has ever explained what it is actually holding up.}

{The arithmetic says nothing can live here by 2012.|They keep saying the world ends in 2012.|Word is the deadline on all of this is 2012.} {That is eleven years, and people are still buying land.|Everyone mentions it, nobody moves house.|Nobody has done a thing about it either way.}

{The archivists set a checkpoint on the square again.|The Foundation held the gate queue to publish people's messages.|The Guild sent somebody down to settle it, they say.} {They read your letters and print them, so be dull and they lose interest.|The Collective wants everything priced and the archive wants it public.|The Guild is two halves that hate each other, so ask which one came.}

{Somebody in the district is selling bullets coated in Fantablack.|There is Fantablack on the market again.|A dealer came through with a case of Fantablack rounds.} {The stuff kills inside a loop, which honest lead does not.|Nobody will say where it was mined.|Ask no questions about the price.}
